https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4545.text: The Foreign Ministry condemns any attacks on civilians, civilian infrastructure or diplomatic missions anywhere in the world that are protected under international law. The Ministry issued this statement on social media in response to Friday's (24 July) Russian attack on the town of Sloviansk in Ukraine. "Slovakia has long been calling for an end to the war in Ukraine, for which there is no military solution; we therefore fully support the peace efforts, which are absolutely essential," stated the Ministry. Both Ukraine and Russia launched further attacks against each other on Friday, resulting in several casualties on both sides. Kyiv attacked the Russian city of Kirov, which is located more than 1,000 kilometres behind the front line. Moscow launched an attack on Kyiv region. The city of Sloviansk in Donetsk region was also targeted by the Russian attack, where five people were killed and the premises of the Latvian Honorary Consulate were damaged. Source: TASR

https://telex.hu/sport/2026/09/26/toth-b.text: Menü Kereső Tóth Balázs: Nagyon csalódottak vagyunk, mert többet érdemeltünk volna Sport Klág Dávid Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Nagyon csalódottak vagyunk, mert többet érdemeltünk volna. Az ellenfélnek összesen két helyzete volt, nekünk viszont a mérkőzés elején megvoltak a lehetőségeink a gólszerzésre” – nyilatkozta Tóth Balázs, a magyar válogatott kapusa, miután 0-1-re kikapott a csapat Ukrajnától a Nemzetek Ligája pénteki mérkőzésén, írja az MTI. Tóth szerint többet érdemelt volna a csapat a vereségnél. A kapus a 77. percben nagyot mentett, amikor szögletre tolta Ihor Krasznopir lövését, de utólag belátja, hogy „semmit sem ért” a védése, „mert azért nem járt pont”. Pénteken két újonc mutatkozott be a válogatottban, Tóth Milán a szünetben, Jurek Gábor a 62. percben lépett pályára. Előbbi csatár kiemelte a Puskás Aréna fantasztikus atmoszféráját, aztán kitért az 55. percben kihagyott helyzetére is, amelynél egyenlíthetett volna a magyar válogatott – írja az MTI. „Magasan jött a labda, és úgy éreztem, ha leveszem, az ellenfél odaér, ezért egyből ellőttem, így viszont sípcsonttal találtam el, és a kapus könnyen védett” – részletezte a Vasas 24 éves támadója, aki elismerte, a második félidőben sem sikerült az ukrán védelem mögé kerülni, pedig megpróbálták a széleken is, egy az egy elleni párharcokban, illetve a beadásokkal, de a labda valahogy nem találta meg a támadókat. A magyarok a második fordulóban az északírekkel találkoznak Belfastban közép-európai idő szerint hétfőn 20.45-től. A magyar futballválogatott rengeteg helyzetet összehozott a Puskás Arénában, de 1-0-ra kikapott Ukrajnától a Nemzetek Ligája B divíziójának első fordulójában. A mérkőzés utolsó percei botrányos jeleneteket hoztak, egymásnak esett a két csapat. A meccsről írt összefoglalónkat itt lehet elolvasni. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Cars drive through a flooded road during a nor'easter storm where a voluntary evacuation has been issued in the community on 26 September 2026 in Point Pleasant, New Jersey. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Cars drive through a flooded road during a nor'easter storm where a voluntary evacuation has been issued in the community on 26 September 2026 in Point Pleasant, New Jersey. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images US weather Nor’easter storm batters US east coast with heavy winds and power outages At least one person killed and nearly 150,000 households lost electricity from North Carolina to New England Marina Dunbar Sun 27 Sep 2026 12.01 EDT Last modified on Sun 27 Sep 2026 12.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A strong, deadly storm known as a nor’easter battered the US’s east coast over the weekend, bringing power outages, flooding, damaging winds and hazardous ocean conditions. Trees and power lines were knocked down across the region, at least one person was killed and hundreds of thousands were left without electricity as officials cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further. There was significant coastal flooding, rough surf, powerful winds, rain and dangerous rip currents from North Carolina through New England. Boston and the New York City tri-state area were among the regions affected. View image in fullscreen Waves crash over homes on Rebecca Road during a nor’easter on 26 September in Scituate, Massachusetts. Photograph: Scott Eisen/Getty Images Power outages by Sunday were already widespread, with nearly 150,000 households losing electricity so far, according to the website Poweroutage.US . The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) advised travelers to check with their airlines for updated flight information. FlightAware reported more than 3,000 US delays and nearly 430 cancellations. Major storm in US north-east knocks out power for 100,000 and floods roads Read more As a result of the storm, New York’s governor, Kathy Hochul, declared a state of emergency covering the Bronx, Kings, Nassau, New York, Queens, Richmond, Suffolk and Westchester counties. A fallen tree in the east New York City borough of Brooklyn resulted in a death on Saturday during the nor’easter. A 56-year-old New York City housing authority employee was killed when a tree came down on him in a parking lot. Police said he was pronounced dead at Brookdale University hospital. Authorities had not immediately determined whether wind caused the tree to fall. In Queens, high winds caused widespread disruption after a tree fell at about 5.40pm in the Glendale area, with downed power lines forcing authorities to close the roadway. As a precaution, the New York City fire department evacuated a nearby building. No injuries were reported in that incident. View image in fullscreen Crews work to clear fallen trees from the property of Burnet Hill’s Haunted Ridge after a nor’easter storm in Livingston, New Jersey, on Saturday. Photograph: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/Getty Images Along the Jersey Shore, residents spent Saturday removing debris and cleaning up between periods of high tide after the nor’easter forced flood water into streets and homes near the New Jersey coast. Eight counties in New Jersey remain under a state of emergency issued before the coastal storm arrived. The storm struck the mid-Atlantic and New England over the weekend and was forecast to continue into the early part of this week. As the week continues, flooding was expected to rise and recede along with the tides. The National Weather Service (NWS) expected coastal flooding to bring significant flooding from the Jersey Shore south to the northern Outer Banks of North Carolina, with more moderate flooding forecast along the Massachusetts coast. https://redditchstandard.co.uk/news/redd.text: Redditch baker and community champion caught in 13-year mistaken identity ordeal Redditch baker Piotr Galas, who has spent years helping others, just wants an end to mistaken identity nightmare. Image: Redditch Standard Claire Bullivant 15 th Oct, 2026 Updated: 15 th Oct, 2026 0 A WELL-KNOWN Redditch baker who has spent years building his business and supporting his local community has spoken of his exhaustion after reportedly being mistaken for a wanted man more than 20 times. Piotr Galas, 50, is a familiar face to many shoppers in Redditch, where his bakery has become known for its freshly made bread, cakes and particularly popular Polish doughnuts. But behind the counter, the hardworking father and businessman has been dealing with an extraordinary problem which he says has followed him for more than a decade. According to a report published by The Sun, Mr Galas has repeatedly been mistaken for a fugitive suspect who allegedly used his identity after absconding while on bail in connection with a rape allegation dating back to 2012. Despite having no connection to the alleged offence, Mr Galas says he has been arrested more than 20 times since 2013, with the confusion continuing to cause difficulties whenever he travels. His latest encounter with police reportedly took place at Bristol Airport last month, when he returned from a holiday in Sardinia. Officers are understood to have stopped him after his details triggered an alert on their computer system. Mr Galas told The Sun that police informed him Interpol was also looking for him, before eventually comparing his photograph with that of the wanted suspect and allowing him to leave. It was another deeply frustrating experience for a man who says he has spent years trying to establish that he is not the person authorities are seeking. Previous incidents have reportedly involved him being removed from aircraft, detained by armed officers and handcuffed in front of his family. He also claims his home and business premises have been searched. In 2022, he reportedly received £20,000 in compensation from British Transport Police following wrongful arrests, yet the mistaken identity problem appears to have persisted. For someone simply trying to run a business, support his family and get on with everyday life, the repeated incidents have understandably taken their toll. And there is much more to Mr Galas than the extraordinary circumstances which have brought him national attention. Readers of the Redditch Standard may remember his efforts to help families affected by the war in Ukraine. In March 2022, we reported how he launched a fundraising initiative at Redditch Craft Bakery, pledging every penny from sales of his famous doughnuts on a designated Saturday to help people whose lives had been devastated by the conflict. The initiative followed a hugely successful Polish Doughnut Day at his bakery, then situated on Evesham Walk outside the Kingfisher Shopping Centre, when more than 1,000 doughnuts were sold before lunchtime. At the time, he hoped the appeal would raise thousands of pounds for those in desperate need. It was a reminder of the generosity and community spirit that can be found among Redditch’s independent traders, many of whom work long hours while finding time to support others. Mr Galas has spent years serving local customers and building a business in the town, becoming a recognisable part of Redditch’s independent shopping community. Now, instead of being able to concentrate on his family and his bakery, he continues to face uncertainty over whether another journey could result in another encounter with police. The situation raises serious questions about how someone who has repeatedly been identified as the wrong person can apparently continue to be flagged on law enforcement systems. It also raises concerns about the lasting personal consequences of mistaken identity, particularly when the person affected has already spent years attempting to resolve the problem. For Mr Galas, there is a simple wish behind the headlines: to be able to live his life, run his business and travel with his family without the fear of being wrongly detained. And for those in Redditch who know him as the man behind the bakery counter, there is another side to this story worth remembering: a local businessman who has worked hard, served his community and stepped forward to help others when they needed it. The allegations surrounding the mistaken identity were reported by The Sun on October 12. The Redditch Standard has not independently verified the number of arrests, the reported compensation payment or the circumstances of the outstanding warrant. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-deal-.text: They came to discuss AI, but EU leaders spent most of their time during a summit in Dublin on Friday grappling with questions about Ukraine — namely who should represent them in future peace talks. Despite plenty of disagreement about whether it should be a single person (and if so, who) or a collection of them, they managed to strike a deal: Future talks would involve national security officials from Germany, France, the U.K., Italy and Poland — the so-called E5 powers — plus representatives from the European Commission and European Council. A classic European compromise. “It is essential to have a team and to speak with one voice,” European Council President António Costa said after the summit, noting that Donald Trump had also tasked two envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, with conducting negotiations. Advertisement Advertisement Ireland, which holds the EU’s rotating presidency and hosted the informal gathering, had billed the meeting as a rare chance for a high-level discussion on how to develop artificial intelligence in accordance with European values. But the question of how to secure peace in Ukraine — and who should negotiate on Europe’s behalf — quickly dominated discussions, as leaders sparred over the format of future peace negotiations and warned about the risks of a potential deal brokered between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Indeed, a meeting next week between the U.S. and Russian leaders has set Europe on edge, prompting warnings about a possible Yalta-type agreement in which superpowers would decide on European security questions over the heads of countries directly concerned, reminiscent of talks toward the end of World War II that divided Europe up between the four allied powers. UAE’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al-Nahyan, members of the Ukrainian and Russian delegations hold talks mediated by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff Jared Kushner in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026. | Pool photo by Altaf Qadri/AFP via Getty Images “That is why I want to make our message to the U.S. very clear: Please, no surprises!” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said regarding the Trump-Putin meeting, scheduled to take place during an APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19. “Continue to play on Team Europe and on the same team as Ukraine. And let’s work together for genuine peace in Ukraine.” The question of who should represent Europe in future discussions about Ukraine and the post-conflict security order was added to the summit’s agenda at the last minute, following a request from Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Earlier in the day, Merz had voiced preference for a narrower group made up of officials from Berlin, Paris and London, while Kaja Kallas, the EU’s chief diplomat, argued that she was best placed to lead discussions. Advertisement Advertisement “I know that the Russians don’t want me, but do we have a say on who is representing Russia? No, we don’t,” said Kallas. “We have a really strong team,” she went on. “I’m ready to do this work with foreign ministers.” AI jockeys with Russia fears It wasn’t all about Ukraine. Over a lunch of baked salmon fillets and crushed Ballymackenny potatoes, EU leaders grappled with the question of how to make AI more “sovereign” — that is, less dependent on U.S. and Chinese technology providers. “Our independence cannot be outsourced, it must be built here at home,” Macron wrote in a post on X in which he also announced that France and the Netherlands would host a meeting of “Tech Creators” on Dec. 2. Amid a global outage of Microsoft software (since resolved), Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch urged leaders to direct some €260 billion currently spent on foreign technology toward home-grown tech infrastructure, research and development. While the bloc has solid foundations on which to build AI solutions, Europe needs “speed, financing and a strong coordination between member states,” said Mensch. But the AI discussion quickly ceded ground to existential questions about Ukraine, including how the bloc would finance Kyiv in coming months and whether Europe would get a seat at the table in upcoming rounds of Ukraine-Russia talks brokered by the U.S. Advertisement Advertisement Just as leaders including Ukraine’s president were gathering in Dublin, Russian President Vladimir Putin said he was open to Europeans joining the talks, reversing Moscow’s previous opposition. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov quickly followed up with qualifications, however, stating that Europeans must first demonstrate “genuine intention and readiness to contribute to the peace process” before being admitted — a condition that Kallas quickly dismissed as a “trap.” “If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us, which is that we divert attention away from that there is no ceasefire,” she told reporters in Dublin. Other officials said that Russia’s preconditions for allowing Europe to join the talks would mean concessions to Moscow’s war demands, namely a withdrawal of NATO from European states bordering Russia, the lifting of sanctions and a ban on foreign troops in Ukraine. Giorgio Leali, Pieter Haeck, Sebastian Starcevic, Caroline Hug and Shawn Pogatchnik contributed to this article from Dublin.

https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/gov.text: The Budapest Times Government releases communist-era secret service files after 36-year delay The government is rectifying an omission from the 1990 democratic transition by releasing the secret service files, the Prime Minister declared at a Wednesday press conference held in Budapest regarding the publication of intelligence documents. The head of government stressed that the release of the files should be handled with dignity and humanity, but that the state security past represents a social trauma that must be uncovered in order to begin a shared process of healing and reconciliation. Before the press conference, the Prime Minister also checked in from the basement of the Historical Archives of the State Security Services (ÁBTL) and viewed the documents held there. He said that following the collapse of the socialist dictatorship, the records of recruitments and the names of those who maintained the regime had been made public in numerous Central European countries, but that this had not happened in Hungary. Governments had obstructed the release of the files for 36 years, the Prime Minister emphasised. He added that in 1988–89, when the destruction of documents shifted into high gear, state security service employees were sometimes instructed to take the files home. For this reason, Péter Magyar asked anyone who has documents stored at home to hand them in. The Prime Minister highlighted at the press conference that the data coming to light is better discussed than judged. The Prime Minister drew attention to the fact that due to the declassification of files, many families are confronted with difficult information about relatives — in most cases already deceased — connected to those files. Péter Magyar asked everyone to treat the obtained data with dignity and humanity, adding that the government will provide assistance to all those affected in processing the information. The Prime Minister stated that on Wednesday the so-called Form 6 cards, the B-log (i.e. recruitment log), and the H-register (i.e. network register) were uploaded to the website https://nyitottaktak.hu/. The Form 6 card is the registration sheet for network persons; its front page contains the agent’s personal identification data, while the back page contains the most important details relating to the agent’s activities. The processing and uploading of the recruitment dossiers and the remaining data will be completed by 25 February 2027, the memorial day for the victims of communism, he added. The Prime Minister spoke about how seventy years ago, in those very hours, following the suppression of the revolution, many thousands of people lost their lives and were forced to leave their homeland, after which the state security service of the Rákosi regime stepped up to an even higher gear and the number of recruitments surged. He noted that historians and researchers put the number of those recruited during the Rákosi and Kádár regimes at approximately 150,000, of which around 60,000 names have so far been made searchable. Further information is expected in the future, as a government decision has resulted in many new documents being transferred to the historical archive from ministries, institutions, and private individuals, he said. The prime minister stated that the disclosure of agent files had become one of the important but ultimately broken promises of the 1990 transition, and that even then it was clear that a democratic, functioning, and free Hungary could not be built without uncovering the state security past. He noted that the democratic opposition that came to power after the transition — contrary to its commitments — had not broadly revealed the state security past, and that although the Duna-gate scandal that broke in February 1990 exposed the Kádár-era secret service’s surveillance of the opposition and the destruction of documents, the transitional elite had let the people down. The greatest responsibility for this lay with the Fidesz-KDNP government, which between 2010 and 2026 had voted down proposals to disclose the files on twenty-five occasions, he recalled. He recalled that the screening law of the Antall government had applied to a narrow group, leaving the network as a whole concealed; that later, following the scandal over Péter Medgyesi’s secret service past, the socialist-liberal government had arrived at a half-measure — the archive was expanded, but public access to documents was kept within narrow limits, providing ample opportunity to conceal important records. He said that 20th-century Hungarian history is full of traumas such as the Treaty of Trianon, the World Wars, the Holocaust, the expulsion of Germans, and the recruitment of more than a hundred thousand people into the secret services. These must not be swept under the rug, but brought to light, so that a shared process of healing and reconciliation can begin, he said. According to the Prime Minister, the agent files are not only a matter for politicians, intellectuals, and the press — the Rákosi and Kádár regimes permeated the whole of Hungarian society. He mentioned that in 1957, in Gyula, a 17-year-old trainee teacher was threatened and recruited because he had protested against the poor quality of food in the dormitory. In Pécel, the school principal of the time was expected to report on the teaching staff and students; in Kecskéd, a village priest was even reported on for what the children talked about during religious education classes, he listed. The network of the dictatorship was present in schools, factories, agricultural cooperatives, churches, among neighbours, and within families, he said. “One of the gravest consequences of how the system operated is that people often could not trust their own colleagues, friends, or family members — tens and hundreds of thousands lived without any idea of who was watching them or who might be reporting on them,” he declared. At the press conference, the Prime Minister described the delay shown by the former political elite in releasing the files as unforgivable, saying that the procrastination had the serious consequence of only a partial disclosure now. He noted that Tisza had already committed to making the files public before the election, and that after coming to power, the National Assembly passed the necessary legislation on 15 September — without the votes of the former political elite. He said the review of still-classified documents is also continuing; however, files and data relating to Department III/I — that is, intelligence — will not be made public. Péter Magyar justified the decision on the grounds that Hungarian national security still has interests in this regard, and that making them public could cause “very serious international and other problems” for the country. Regarding the publicly available and researchable files, the prime minister stressed that the greatest responsibility lies with those who created and shaped the state security system: the party leaders of the Rákosi and Kádár regimes, the service commanders who organised the surveillance, the case officers who directed the recruitment operations and blackmailed, paid, or threatened the recruited individuals. “The Hungarian state is handing over to Hungarian society the information over which it exercised exclusive control for decades,” said Péter Magyar, who also asked those wishing to learn about their own or their family’s history to make use of this opportunity. The prime minister asked journalists, public figures, and historians to use the information being made public with particular responsibility — to verify the original documents, examine the historical circumstances, seek the views of those concerned, and to claim no more than what the documents support. He pointed out that what happened must be processed primarily in the communities most affected: in families, among circles of friends, and in small communities. In response to a journalist’s question about what the review committee led by János Rainer M. is working on and since when, Péter Magyar said: the body, which is already active, can review and revise the classification designations of the intelligence services — meaning it can help bring further data into the public domain. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/.text: Un incendiu a izbucnit, duminică seara, la Hotelul Alpin din Poiana Braşov, pompierii intervenind cu mai multe autospeciale pentru a preveni extinderea focului. Forţele de intervenţie au fost suplimentate din judeţele Prahova, Covasna şi Argeş. Aproximativ 150 de persoane au fost evacuate din clădire, fără a fi înregistrate victime. ACTUALIZARE 23:35 - „Situaţia este sub control. Nu există victime, iar toţi oaspeţii şi membrii personalului sunt în siguranţă”, anunţă conducerea hotelului. Conform sursei citate, la nivelul terasei unui apartament superior al Hotelului Alpin din Poiana Braşov a izbucnit un incendiu. „Datorită intervenţiei prompte şi profesioniste a echipajelor ISU Braşov, incendiul a fost stabilizat, iar echipele de intervenţie continuă operaţiunile necesare pentru eliminarea oricărui risc. Colaborăm îndeaproape cu autorităţile competente. Cauzele incendiului vor fi stabilite în urma verificărilor de specialitate. Mulţumim echipajelor ISU Braşov, serviciilor de urgenţă şi tuturor celor implicaţi pentru mobilizarea exemplară, profesionalismul şi rapiditatea cu care au acţionat. Regretăm disconfortul şi îngrijorarea provocate şi vă asigurăm de întreaga noastră responsabilitate şi implicare. Siguranţa oamenilor a fost, este şi va rămâne întotdeauna prioritatea noastră absolută”, este mesajul postat pe Facebook de conducerea hotelului. ACTUALIZARE 23:00 - Potrivit ISU Braşov, în prezent, incendiul se manifestă la nivelul acoperişului, mansardei şi ultimelor trei etaje ale clădirii, pe o suprafaţă de aproximativ 2.000 de metri pătraţi. „În urma producerii incendiului, aproximativ 150 de persoane au fost evacuate din interiorul clădirii. Din fericire, până la acest moment, nu s-au înregistrat victime”, a adăugat sursa citată. Potrivit ISU Braşov, incendiul se manifestă la nivelul mansardei şi al faţadei clădirii, pe o suprafaţă de aproximativ 300 de metri pătraţi. „Din informaţiile primite la acest moment, nu ar fi persoane surprinse în interiorul clădirii”, a precizat sursa citată. Foto: Inquam Photos / Alex Nicodim Deschide galeria foto Acolo au fost mobilizate forţe şi mijloace de intervenţie din cadrul ISU Braşov, SVSU Râşnov, ISU Covasna, ISU Prahova şi ISU Argeş, precum şi echipaje ale Serviciului de Ambulanţă Judeţean. La locul intervenţiei acţionează 11 autospeciale de stingere, patru autoscări, o autospecială de hidroperforare, un autocamion de intervenţie, două echipaje de prim ajutor SMURD și trei echipaje ale Serviciului de Ambulanţă Judeţean. Potrivit ISU, intervenţia este în desfăşurare, iar echipajele operative acţionează pentru localizarea şi lichidarea incendiului, precum şi pentru protejarea persoanelor şi a construcţiilor învecinate.
